newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan rate shouldn't be raised for 3-4 months-Jiji.
newsitem.headline: Japan rate shouldn't be raised for 3-4 months-Jiji.

text.p: Jiro Ushio, chairman of the Japan Association of Corporate Executives, told a news conference on Tuesday that Japan's official discount rate should not be raised in the coming three to four months, Jiji news agency reported.
"There are views among manufacturers that it would be OK to raise the interest rate, but weaker firms are being supported by low interest rates," Jiji quoted Ushio as saying.
"It's difficult to say to what degree (the rate should be raised), but it should not be raised in the coming three to four months," he said.
The Japan Association of Corporate Executives groups corporate executives who join as individuals, not as a company. It is one of the four major business associations in Japan.
